title: Stable conormal comparison at a prime for a concrete complete intersection presentation
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n,m,t\in\mathbf N$, $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $Q=k[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $I\subseteq P$ be an ideal, $S=P/I$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $\mathfrak q$ a prime of $S$, and $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$. Put $S_g=S[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $f:\{1,\ldots,t\}\to Q$, $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$, assume $t\le m$, and let $e:Q/J\xrightarrow{\sim}S_g$ be a $k$-algebra isomorphism. Assume $\dim\operatorname{Spec}(S_g)=m-t$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define the conormal $S$-module $I/I^2$ with the quotient scalar action, $N=(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and $R=S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then there exists an $R$-linear isomorphism $N\oplus R^m\cong R^{t+n}$, where $R^a$ denotes the module of functions from a set of $a$ elements to $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), last paragraph of proof of (1) => (4), through the stable conormal equation from Lemma 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize); successive localization made explicit. Source checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00SC and /tag/00S6 on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Extend q to the prime p=qS_g and identify (S_g)_p with S_q using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso]. Pull p back through e and the quotient Q → Q/J to p′. Since p exists, S_g and Q/J are nonzero. The spectrum homeomorphism induced by e transfers the dimension identity to Q/J; t ≤ m makes it the additive dimension identity dim Spec(Q/J)+t=m.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] to f at p′, which contains J. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] to these images in Q_p′ to obtain a basis of length t for JQ_p′/(JQ_p′)² over Q_p′/JQ_p′.

Localize the quotient sequence 0 → J² → J → J/J² → 0 at Q∖p′ and use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Localization commutes with products of ideals, so J²Q_p′=(JQ_p′)². Localizing 0 → J → Q → Q/J → 0 identifies the scalar quotient with (Q/J) at the corresponding prime, hence through e with (S_g)_p and through step 1 with S_q. The quotient actions agree since all identifications send the class of rx to the scalar r times the class of x. Therefore the localized J/J² is S_q-linearly isomorphic to S_q^t.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-module-principal-localization] to the quotient map α : k[x] → S and β : Q → Q/J → S_g. The kernels identify with I and J, compatibly with their quotient scalar actions. Localize the resulting equivalence at p; localization preserves finite products and linear equivalences. The iterated localization of I/I² identifies with its localization at q: (x/g^a)/(s/g^b) maps to g^b x/(g^a s), and its vanishing says that some g^c s outside q annihilates the numerator. These fraction maps are inverse and respect the scalar isomorphism of step 1. Substitute the equivalence with S_q^t of step 3 and combine S_q^t × S_q^n via Fin(t+n) ≃ Fin t ⊕ Fin n. This gives N × S_q^m ≃ S_q^(t+n).
